title: Pakistan Codes & Standards
intro: Pakistan-specific codes and limits that PPSC, FPSC, KPPSC and WAPDA papers ask about. Values were checked against the gazette notifications, PEC and PSQCA sources listed at the end. Provinces now issue their own environmental standards (PEQS, SEQS, KP-EQS) after the 18th Amendment — quote the national value unless the paper names a province.

chapters.t: Building Code of Pakistan (BCP) — The Family of Codes
b: Issued after the 8 October 2005 Kashmir earthquake; compatible with UBC-97, ACI 318-05 and AISC
Prepared by ENERCON (now NEECA) with PEC; adopted from ASHRAE 90.1-2004; mandatory for new non-residential buildings
Electrical and telecom safety in buildings
Prepared by PEC with NDMA; based on NFPA 1 Fire Code
Replaces the 2007 seismic provisions; based on IBC (International Building Code)

Who approves: Building codes are reviewed and notified through the Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC Act 1976) with the Ministry of Housing & Works; enforcement is by the building-control authority of each city (CDA, LDA, KBCA/SBCA, RDA, PDA …).
💡 Exam point: BCP 2007 → UBC-97 basis; BCP 2021 → IBC basis. Fire 2016 → NFPA; Energy 2011 → ASHRAE 90.1.

chapters.t: BCP Seismic Provisions 2007 — Zones & Key Rules
b: Design earthquake: Ground motion with 10% probability of exceedance in 50 years (≈ 475-year return period).
Zoning: Pakistan divided into five seismic zones by peak ground acceleration (PGA), following UBC-97 zoning.

Site (soil) profile types: SA hard rock, SB rock, SC very dense soil/soft rock, SD stiff soil, SE soft soil, SF special soils needing site-specific study. If soil properties are not known, use type SD.
Seismic coefficients: Ca and Cv depend on zone and soil profile type; they define the design response spectrum (as in UBC-97).

Structural systems: Where PGA ≥ 0.2 g, high-ductility systems such as special moment-resisting frames are required; ordinary systems are allowed only where PGA < 0.2 g and the building is low (height ≈ 15 m or less).

Base shear (UBC-97 form): V = Cv·I·W/(R·T), not more than 2.5·Ca·I·W/R and not less than 0.11·Ca·I·W. I = importance factor, R = response modification factor, T = fundamental period, W = seismic weight.
Approximate period: T = Ct·hn^(3/4); Ct = 0.0853 (steel moment frames), 0.0731 (RC moment frames and eccentrically braced frames), 0.0488 (all other buildings), with hn in metres.
💡 Exam point: Unknown soil → profile SD. Zone 4 is the highest (PGA > 0.32 g). Return period of design earthquake ≈ 475 years (10% in 50 years).

Basis: International Building Code (IBC) approach in place of UBC-97: mapped spectral accelerations at short period (Ss) and 1 second (S1), site classes A–F, design spectral values SDS and SD1, and seismic design categories (SDC A–F) instead of zones 1–4.
Site classes: Classified by average shear-wave velocity Vs30 (or SPT N / undrained strength) in the top 30 m, as in ASCE 7.
Load combinations & design: Strength design with ASCE 7–type load combinations; concrete to ACI 318 and steel to AISC (editions referenced in the code).
💡 Exam point: If a question says "seismic design category" or "Ss and S1" it refers to BCP 2021/IBC; "Zone 2B, Ca, Cv" refers to BCP 2007/UBC-97.

NEQS for municipal and liquid industrial effluents were first approved by the Pakistan Environmental Protection Council in 1993 and revised in 2000 (SRO 549(I)/2000). Values in mg/L unless stated; three columns: into inland waters / into sewage treatment / into sea.
SC: "Sea concentration" — discharge may not raise the concentration above that of the receiving sea water.
Original 1993 values: BOD 80, COD 150, TSS 150, TDS 3500, pH 6–10, temperature 40 °C — older books still quote these.

Punjab (PEQS): Punjab Environmental Quality Standards give separate columns for municipal and industrial discharges, with some different limits (e.g., TDS 3000 mg/L instead of 3500). Use the national value unless the paper names Punjab.
💡 Exam point: NEQS effluent BOD = 80 mg/L, COD = 150 mg/L (inland waters). WHO has no effluent standard — NEQS/PEQS are local.

chapters.t: National Standards for Drinking Water Quality (NSDWQ) 2010
b: Notified by Pak-EPA in 2010 (SRO 1063(I)/2010, Gazette of 26 November 2010). Values in mg/L unless stated.
Must not be detectable in any 100 mL sample
💡 Exam point: Pakistan arsenic limit 0.05 mg/L (50 ppb) — five times the WHO value of 0.01 mg/L (10 ppb). Lead in NSDWQ is also higher than the WHO value.
Notified with the drinking-water standards in 2010 (SRO 1062(I)/2010). Values in µg/m³ (CO in mg/m³); the stricter column has applied from 1 January 2013.
Earlier (2010) column: PM2.5 25 / 40, PM10 200 / 250, lead 1.5 / 2 — tightened from 2013. SO₂, NO, NO₂ and CO values did not change.

Pakistan Environmental Protection Act (PEPA): 1997 — created Pak-EPA and the Environmental Protection Council; Section 12 requires an IEE or EIA before construction of a project (outer limit for the agency decision: four months).

IEE & EIA Regulations: 2000 — Schedule I projects need an IEE (initial environmental examination), Schedule II projects need a full EIA; the agency decides within 45 days (IEE) and 90 days (EIA) of a complete application.

After 18th Amendment (2010): Environment became a provincial subject: Punjab EPA Act (amended 2012), Sindh EPA Act 2014, KP EPA Act 2014, Balochistan EPA Act 2012 — each with its own standards and review procedure.
💡 Exam point: IEE = smaller projects (Schedule I); EIA = major projects (Schedule II) such as large dams, highways and power plants.
PSQCA: Pakistan Standards & Quality Control Authority (Act VI of 1996) issues Pakistan Standards (PS) and runs compulsory certification for items such as cement.

PS 232: Ordinary Portland cement. The 2008 edition uses grades 43 and 53 (like IS); the 2015 revision uses strength classes 32.5, 42.5 and 52.5 N/R (like EN 197-1). Chemical limits quoted by makers: MgO ≤ 6%, SO₃ ≤ 3%.
PS 5313: Common cements per EN 197-1 (CEM I, CEM II blended types) — printed on many local bags (e.g., CEM II/A-M 42.5N).
Reinforcing bars: Pakistan standard for deformed bars is aligned with ASTM A615; local mills sell Grade 40 (280 MPa) and Grade 60 (420 MPa).
Bricks: Standard first-class burnt clay brick in Pakistan ≈ 9 × 4.5 × 3 in. (nominal).
💡 Exam point: Cement bag "PS 232 Grade 53" = OPC; "PS 5313 CEM II" = blended cement.
NHA General Specifications (1998): Standard technical specification for national highways; contract BOQs refer to its item numbers.

Marshall criteria commonly specified for wearing course (Item 305): 75 blows each face; stability ≥ 1000 kg; flow 8–14 (units of 0.25 mm); air voids 4–6% (some contracts 4–7%); loss of stability after immersion ≤ 20–25%. Check the project special provisions — values are set per contract.
Compaction (typical): Embankment and subgrade ≥ 95% of modified AASHTO (T-180) maximum dry density; subbase and base ≥ 98–100% of modified AASHTO.
Bitumen grades in Pakistan: Penetration grades 60/70 (hot plains — most common) and 80/100 (cooler northern areas); performance grades (PG) used on newer motorways.
Design references: AASHTO 1993 Guide for pavement thickness (structural number SN), Asphalt Institute MS-2 for Marshall mix design, AASHTO Green Book for geometric design.
💡 Exam point: Item 305 = AC wearing course; Item 203 = asphalt base; Item 202 = aggregate base; Item 201 = subbase.
Islamabad: CDA Building Regulations and the Islamabad Capital Territory zoning regulations.
Karachi / Sindh: Karachi Building & Town Planning Regulations 2002, enforced by the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA).
Punjab (other cities): Punjab Private Housing Schemes and Land Sub-division Rules; Punjab Land Use (Classification, Reclassification and Redevelopment) Rules 2009.

Common items in by-laws: Setbacks (front, rear, side), floor area ratio (FAR), ground coverage, maximum height, parking, structural-stability certificate by a PEC-registered engineer, completion certificate before occupation.
💡 Exam point: FAR = total covered area of all floors ÷ plot area. Ground coverage = ground-floor covered area ÷ plot area.
PEC Standard Form of Bidding Documents: Based on FIDIC conditions of contract; mandatory for many public-sector civil works contracts.
PEC contractor categories: Constructors are licensed in categories C-A (no cost limit), C-B, and C-1 to C-6 (decreasing contract-value limits); limits are revised by PEC.
Procurement rules: Federal: Public Procurement Rules 2004 (PPRA Ordinance 2002). Punjab: Punjab Procurement Rules 2014 (PPRA Punjab). Sindh: SPP Rules 2010. KP: KPPRA Rules 2014.
Market Rate System (MRS): Punjab Finance Department publishes district-wise market rates of materials and labour twice a year; used with the Schedule of Rates to prepare estimates.
Schedule of Rates: Composite Schedule of Rates (CSR) — Punjab and other provinces; Pak PWD Schedule of Rates for federal works.
💡 Exam point: Estimates in Punjab = CSR item rates updated with the current MRS rates.
